description: Given an integer array nums, return an integer array counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i].
intuition: Merge sort naturally counts inversions - elements that are out of order. During the merge step, when a right-side element gets placed first, it tells you how many left-side elements are larger (i.e., have smaller elements to their right).
approach: Use merge sort with index tracking. During the merge step, when an element from the right half is placed before elements from the left half, it contributes to the count of those left-half elements.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: nums = [5,2,6,1]
Initial indices: [0,1,2,3]
mergeSort(0,4):
  mergeSort(0,2): sort [5,2] → indices=[1,0] (2 before 5)
    When placing 5 (idx 0): rightPtr-mid=0 → counts[0]+=0
    But 2 placed first → counts[0]+=1
  mergeSort(2,4): sort [6,1] → indices=[3,2]
    counts[2]+=1 (1 before 6)
  Merge [2,5] with [1,6]:
    1 < 2 → place 1 (idx3)
    2 placed: rightPtr-mid=1 → counts[1]+=1
    5 placed: rightPtr-mid=1 → counts[0]+=1
    6 placed as remainder
counts = [2,1,1,0]
explanation:
1. Track original indices through the merge sort.
2. During merge, when placing a left element, all right elements already placed (j - mid) are smaller.
3. Add j - mid to the count for that left element.
4. After merge sort, counts[i] holds the number of smaller elements to the right of index i.
hints: Track original indices so you can update the correct count.
When merging, the number of right-side elements already placed tells you how many are smaller.
